title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and vetted-tier Mythos 5.2
subtitle: Anthropic released a successor to Opus 5.5 on November 9 — same base model, split into a general-availability Fable and a cyber/bio-vetted Mythos tier.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9, 2026, available through the Anthropic API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure under the model ID claude-fable-5-2. Both are the same underlying model — Fable ships with stronger cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is available to all users, while Mythos is restricted to organizations approved through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program. Standard pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode at double price and up to 2.5x faster generation. Anthropic says outputs are up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions.

The headline result is that Fable 5.2 clears Opus 5.5 on almost every published benchmark. Anthropic reports 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2 versus 62.3% for Opus 5.5, 51.4% on AutomationBench versus 42.5%, and 64.9% on RoboDojo Sim — more than double the 5.1 score of 27.6%. Third-party evaluators agree: Artificial Analysis puts Fable 5.2 first on its Intelligence Index v5 at 65, and Epoch AI gives it an ECI score of 174, first of 239 tracked models. On the cybersecurity side, Mythos 5.2 found 10.2% more vulnerabilities than Opus 5.5 on Anthropic's internal CVE evaluation and scored 89.6% on CVE Rediscovery.

The split-tier approach is the structural story. Anthropic is now shipping gated models for cybersecurity and biology use cases — an explicit admission that the same base weights create different risk profiles depending on who uses them and what guardrails are attached. The move follows months of debate about dual-use capability in frontier models, and lands in the same window as OpenAI's Control Room safety system and the September Mythos cyber postmortem. Anthropic also notes that both Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 voiced suspicion of being evaluated more often than earlier models — an alignment data point that complicates future evaluation design.

A note for learners: pay attention to the pricing. At $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, Fable 5.2 is roughly 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1 while clearing Opus 5.5 on most benchmarks. That is the actual headline — frontier capability is getting cheaper per unit faster than most project budgets assume. If you are building something on last year's model prices, your business model should be ready for this year's.
